title: How Muse Image draws
description: Meta's image model plans first, then draws and checks. And why one prompt gives a new picture every time.

steps.text: Most of the illustrations in these lessons were drawn by Muse Image, Meta's image model. It doesn't take ready-made pictures from the internet. Every time, it draws something new from a text description — a prompt.

steps.definition: Muse Image first plans the composition — what goes where — then draws and checks its draft. If something doesn't match the prompt, it fixes that part or redraws the whole picture.
steps.example: Prompt: “a cat on a windowsill in the rain.” Plan: window, cat, raindrops. Check: no raindrops? Add them.

steps.imagePrompt: A robot artist at an easel making a rough pencil sketch of a cat on a windowsill, with the finished colorful painting of the same scene standing next to it.
steps.caption: First a plan, then a drawing, then a check
Step through the picture's path, then run it again: same prompt, new picture

steps.text: Did you notice? The same prompt gives a new picture every time. That's not a glitch: image generation has some randomness in it, like temperature in text models. So for a series of pictures in one style, you write the style into the prompt itself. That's how the illustrations for these lessons were made.

How do you write a prompt for a picture? Describe the scene: who, where, doing what, and the mood. Name the style. Say what you don't want — for example, “no text.” Letters in generated pictures often come out with mistakes.

steps.situation: You're drawing five pictures for a presentation, and they all come out in different styles.
options: Describe the same style in every prompt
Repeat the request until the style matches by chance
Ask it to “do it like last time”
steps.explain: The model doesn't remember earlier pictures. A shared style holds only if it's written into every prompt.

steps.text: The “Draw it for me” button on lesson pictures works the same way. The app takes the step's prompt and adds the “about you” note from your profile — only that, plus the language. Your name, age and gender stay on the phone. Muse Image redraws the same idea around your life.

steps.question: Why does every picture cost money, even one you didn't like?
steps.answer: The model did all the work: it planned, drew and checked. You pay for the generation, not for the result. That's why the illustrations for the lessons were drawn in advance and ship inside the app: showing them is free and works offline.

steps.text: In short. Muse Image is a reasoning model: it plans the composition, draws, and checks itself. One prompt gives a new picture every time, so you write the style of a series into every prompt. Every generation costs money — even one you didn't like.

questions.q: What does Muse Image do before it draws?
options: Plans the composition of the scene
Looks for a similar picture online
Draws right away, with no plan
questions.explain: First a plan — what goes where — then the drawing and a check.

questions.q: Why does one prompt give different pictures?
options: The model updates itself every time
Generation has some randomness in it
The model avoids repeating the last one
questions.explain: As with text models, picture generation has randomness in it.

questions.q: What is sent to the model by the “Draw it for me” button?
options: Your name, age and profile photo
The step's prompt, “about you” and language
questions.explain: Only the step's prompt, your “about you” note and the language. Everything else stays on the phone.
